title: The Veil of Ironhollow
premise: August Villalobos, an exiled storm-caller hiding as a charm-seller in Ironhollow, learns the border wards fell because the king's crown is a hollowed vessel for a memory-eating entity called the Unremembered. As stars vanish and citizens forget their own names, August must journey to the capital with a ward-keeper's daughter who remembers too much and a disgraced royal cartographer. He discovers the entity was once his own mentor, bound into the crown by August's exile decree twelve years ago. In the throne room, August cannot destroy the entity without erasing every memory of himself from the world; he chooses to let it consume him, but the people he saved carry him forward in story rather than memory, and he returns changed—no longer invisible, no longer quite himself.
about_author: Silas Pemberton is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing forgotten municipal records in northern England before turning to fantasy. They write about memory, exile, and the quiet violence of being overlooked.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: August's POV. Selling charms in Ironhollow's night market, August feels the border wards snap like cut harp strings just as the stars extinguish overhead. A customer pays with a coin bearing the king's face—and the face is blank. The beat is dread disguised as routine: August realizes his careful invisibility has ended, whether he moves or not.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: August's POV. Wren Calloway, daughter of the dead ward-keeper, finds August's shop carrying her father's ledger—which names August as the storm-caller whose exile funded the wards. She remembers everything the city is forgetting. The emotional beat is reluctant alliance: two people who survive by hiding, forced to trust.

chapters.title: What the Wards Were For
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Reading her father's ledger, Wren learns the wards didn't keep enemies out—they kept the king's crown sealed in. Her father died reinforcing them. August confesses fragments of his exile. The beat is grief and guilt: protection built on secrets fails everyone at once.

chapters.title: The Cartographer of Missing Roads
chapters.summary: August's POV. In the drowned quarter they recruit Odell Brack, a royal cartographer erased from court records, whose maps show roads that only exist when remembered aloud. He agrees to guide them to the capital if they'll speak his name daily so he doesn't fade. The beat is fragile hope through found company.

chapters.title: Hollow Country
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Crossing emptied villages where residents smile vacantly, mid-name, the trio encounters a child who has forgotten her mother but not her fear. August uses storm-calling for the first time in twelve years to shield them from a forgetting-fog. The beat is terror and reawakening: his power costs him memories of home.

chapters.title: The Mentor in the Mirror
chapters.summary: August's POV. Sheltering in a ruined academy, August finds his old master Aldous Vane's journals revealing Vane voluntarily bound himself into the crown to stop a war—using August's exile decree as the binding key. August understands: he is the lock. The beat is devastating recognition that his punishment was someone else's sacrifice.

chapters.title: The City That Forgot Its King
chapters.summary: Odell's POV. Entering the capital, they find pageants celebrating a king no one can describe, guards obeying orders from an empty throne room. Odell maps the palace from childhood memory while it literally reshapes around them. The beat is uncanny dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Audience with the Hollow Crown
chapters.summary: August's POV. In the throne room, the Unremembered wears King Aldric like a glove and offers August a bargain: his old life restored, exile revoked, if he walks away. It shows him visions of the family who forgot him. The beat is temptation at its most human—the longing to belong offered by the thing that un-belonging created.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren and Odell hold the palace gates against forgetting-fog while August begins the unbinding, reciting his own true name—the one thing the entity cannot digest. Storm and silence war over the city. The climax beat is self-erasure as courage: August lets the entity take his memories to free the king, trusting others to remember for him.

chapters.title: Carried in Story
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, rotating briefly. The king wakes; the stars return one by one. August survives but remembers nothing of himself—yet Wren tells him his story each morning, Odell draws his face in every map margin, and slowly new memories accrete around the old shape. The final beat is belonging rebuilt: identity as something we make together, not something we keep.
